subject: EvalConnect POC — implementation playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@greenwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: EvalConnect POC — implementation playbook & next steps

Evan / Priya — great conversation earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

1) POC goal (agreed): Validate integration of Redwood Inference into EvalConnect pipeline to reduce inference latency for batch scoring from ~250ms/token to <120ms/token and measure token-level cost delta.

2) Success criteria (draft): 
   - End-to-end latency: median per-request latency under 150ms for 512-token average payloads (90th < 250ms)
   - Cost: per-1M tokens cost reduced by >= 20% vs current managed endpoint with caching disabled
   - Functional: model outputs match baseline fidelity for the 3 evaluation sets (fraud-detect, entity-normalize, sentiment-enrich) with <2% regression in core metrics

3) Scope & timeline: 3-week trial (Mon May 3 — Fri May 21)
   - Week 0 (prep): API keys, network allowlist, sample payloads, and test harness access
   - Week 1: SDK/shopper integration + streaming proof of concept for long-chat scoring
   - Week 2: KV cache and batching configuration + load run
   - Week 3: Quality validation, cost analysis, and exec summary

4) Owners: 
   - Redwood primary: Marcus Lin (sales) — overall coordination
   - Redwood technical: Neha Kapoor (solutions eng) — SDK snippets, infra checklist, runbook
   - Customer: Evan Ross (platform lead) — env access, test harness, sample datasets

5) Implementation highlights (initial ask from Neha): 
   - Confirm SDK language (we recommended python + node)
   - Provide streaming vs non-streaming routes to compare latency
   - Enable a staging model variant with smaller context window for cost tests

Attachments: gw-eval-success-criteria.xlsx (success matrix), redwood-sdk-integration-snippets.md (snippets), integration-diagram.png

Next actions (Marcus): I'll send the draft playbook + a short runbook for your infra team today. Evan — can you confirm: do you have a VPC peer or IP allowlist we should add, and which test harness will you expose (hosted endpoint vs internal queue)?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mobile: (415) 555-0172

From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@greenwave.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@greenwave.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EvalConnect POC — implementation playbook & next steps

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. Couple quick confirmations from our side: 

- We can run the timeline you proposed. May 3 start is fine. 
- We'll provide a staging cluster with IP allowlist (I will send the CIDR range by COB Monday). 
- Test harness: we'll expose an internal HTTP queue (auth token) and a separate S3 location for batch jobs. For streaming tests, we can stand up a websocket proxy in front of the queue.

Two asks: 
1) Can Redwood provide a lightweight example that shows token-level cost reporting (ideally per-request breakdown) so our finance team can follow along?
2) For the fidelity checks, we have three evaluation sets; can you assign one Redwood SME to own the metric mapping? We want a single point of contact.

I'll loop in Priya for the schedule windowing — she'll own the internal infra setup. 

Evan
Platform Lead | GreenWave Analytics
E: evan.ross@greenwave.ai

Thanks Evan — answers inline below and attaching the runbook+snippets. 

1) Token-level cost reporting: we'll provide a small billing helper that logs per-request token counts + cost estimate (attached: redwood-sdk-integration-snippets.md). That will emit a CSV you can ingest into finance.

2) SME for metrics: assigning Neha to be the metric owner for the trial. She'll coordinate mapping between your eval sets and Redwood's output fields.

Operational items for your infra team (Neha): 
- Please provide the allowlist CIDRs and the auth token format. We'll provide a temporary API key with scoped read/write for the trial window.
- For streaming tests we recommend using our /v1/streams endpoint (websocket) and a fallback /v1/generate route for non-streamed comparison. Snippets attached.

Attached files: gw-eval-success-criteria.xlsx, redwood-sdk-integration-snippets.md, integration-diagram.png

Proposed quick cadence: 30-minute kickoff on May 3 (10:00 PDT) — can Priya or Evan confirm?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@greenwave.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@greenwave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: EvalConnect POC — implementation playbook & next steps

Evan / Priya — quick technical checklist before kickoff. I will be on the May 3 call and owned metrics mapping as discussed. Please try to get these to us by Apr 28 so we can provision and test credentials in the prep week: 

- Network: CIDR blocks for allowlist + any proxy TLS interception to be disclosed
- Auth: preferred token format (Bearer vs mTLS) and token rotation cadence
- Payloads: representative JSON payloads (single request and batch manifest) + average token estimates
- Test data: location of the 3 evaluation sets in S3 (we need read-only links)
- Expected QPS for the load run (we'll simulate 50/100/200 QPS profiles)

Tech notes for your infra team (short): 
- SDKs we will push: python (requests + streaming helper) and node (fetch + eventsource). Example endpoints: 
   - Non-stream: POST https://api.redwood.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   - Stream: wss://streams.redwood.redwood.ai/v1/streams
- For streaming latency parity tests, send chunking sizes of ~128 tokens to mirror production chunking.

If you prefer, I can share a short terraform snippet to provision ephemeral test keys.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
